title: System Tray, Bundling & Capabilities
objectives: Outline bundling without network at runtime
Design tray behavior that respects lifecycle
body:
# Tray, Bundling & Capabilities

## Capabilities = the security contract

```json
{
  "identifier": "default",
  "windows": ["main"],
  "permissions": ["core:default"]
}
```

This app grants ONLY core defaults. No shell, no broad fs, no http plugin.
Every privileged action is an app command that validates input. Adding a
plugin later means adding its permission here — a reviewable diff, not ambient
power. **Least privilege is a design input, not an afterthought.**

## Bundling offline

- `frontendDist: ../dist` — Vite output (Monaco chunks included) embedded.
- Curriculum compiled into the binary via `include_dir`.
- Bundle targets intentionally empty in dev config → raw exe, no installer
  downloads; production adds platform targets explicitly.

After install: zero network. CSP even forbids remote origins (`default-src
'self'`), so accidental fetches fail loudly in development.

## System tray patterns

```rust
// concept — v2 tray API via tauri::tray::TrayIconBuilder
TrayIconBuilder::new()
    .menu(&menu)               // Show / Hide / Quit
    .on_menu_event(|app, ev| match ev.id().as_ref() {
        "quit" => app.exit(0),
        _ => {}
    })
```

Rules: menu mirrors window state; Quit exits fully (no zombie background
tasks); tray actions reuse the same services commands use — no second logic
path.

## Update-less by design
No auto-update fetches: versioning ships with content (catalog.version). Users
upgrade deliberately — consistent with offline-first.
